newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering raises 1997 sales, profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Schering raises 1997 sales, profit outlook.

text.p: German drugs group Schering AG on Wednesday said it planned to post a 14 percent rise in sales and double-digit earnings growth in 1997, raising its forecasts from predictions made several weeks ago.

"For the current business year, at current exchange rates, we expect a 14 percent rise in sales to around six billion marks ($3.6 billion). The group profit will grow at just above double-digit rates," Schering chief financial officer Klaus Pohle said.

Growth will be generated primarily by contraceptive and hormone fertility products, Schering said, adding that its diagnostic products would show only a small increase in sales, due to ongoing price pressures.
Pohle however cautioned that the group's 1997 operating profit would be affected by high goodwill writeoffs, taken after the group last year acquired a several new companies.
Schering in February predicted its 1997 sales would grow by about 13 percent while profits were seen rising between eight and nine percent.
For 1996, the world's largest maker of oral contraceptives posted a 13 percent rise in sales to 5.2 billion marks while group profits soared 46 percent to 362 million marks.
